audit: (1) Diagnosis labels are heterogeneous ICD-O style terms: the same entity is split across labels (e.g. 'Rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS' vs 'Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS'; 'Craniopharyngioma' vs the adamantinomatous label; 'Glioma, malignant' vs 'Glioblastoma'), and 1 in 10 cases are 'missing'/'Unknown'/'Neoplasm, NOS' style labels, so 'rest of cohort' comparisons are contaminated and vague-label hits were not reported. (2) Several single-codon variants recur across unrelated diagnoses at implausible rates (C17orf80 p.S281R in 72 cases, HLTF p.Q898E, ZNF510 p.Q248E, CD69 p.L176Q, CD46 p.K388N, CCDC168 p.Q1530*), consistent with germline leakage or pipeline artifacts; I removed them, which raises doubt about overall call quality. (3) A handful of hypermutated tumors (up to ~15,700 calls) inflate long or passenger genes; cases with >1000 calls were excluded. (4) Some statistically strong hits look biologically implausible: scattered, almost entirely missense, non-hotspot mutations in ARID1B in 'Rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS' (16/66), ASXL1 in medulloblastoma (17/212), PIK3R1 in pilocytic astrocytoma (30/168, in very low-burden tumors) and ZMYM3 in malignant glioma (21/170). Their pattern does not match known driver biology (truncating or domain-clustered), so I suspect batch/caller artifacts or label confounding and did not report them, though I cannot rule them out. (5) WES of SNVs/indels misses fusions and copy-number events (KIAA1549-BRAF, PAX3/7-FOXO1, SMARCB1 deletions, MYCN), so frequencies for those entities are underestimates and many diagnoses lack drivers. (6) Many diagnosis groups are tiny (n<=12), so frequency estimates are imprecise, and medulloblastoma is not subgrouped, so subgroup-specific drivers are diluted. BRAF appears as p.V640E (alternate transcript numbering of V600E).
methods: For each diagnosis label I compared the fraction of cases carrying at least one non-synonymous mutation in each gene against all other cases with a one-sided Fisher exact test (hypergeometric, standard library), requiring >=2 mutated cases, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all diagnosis-gene tests. Before testing I excluded cases with >1000 mutation calls (hypermutators) and six recurrent single-codon artifacts seen across unrelated tumor types. I then reviewed the protein changes of each significant hit (hotspots, truncation pattern, mutation burden of carriers) and kept findings that were statistically robust and biologically coherent; probabilities reflect q-value, sample size, and prior plausibility, and expected frequencies are observed rates moderately adjusted toward literature-plausible values.
